_comment: HUMAN-OWNED. Identifiers that belong to a work ORCID already knows about, but which the ORCID record itself does not carry. ORCID frequently holds the DOI and nothing else, which leaves the bibliography with no SciX (formerly ADS) link even for a published paper. The sync never reads or writes this file, so these survive every regeneration of generated/publications.json.
_howToUse: Key on `doi` — the identifier ORCID reliably does have.
`bibcode` FILLS IN a null field, and REPLACES a preprint (arXiv) bibcode once
the paper is published; it never overwrites a journal bibcode ORCID supplied.
`title` overrides ORCID's title — only for casing or typography fixes, never
Verify a bibcode before adding it. Entries added 2026-10-17 come from SciX's
own DOI resolution (scixplorer.org/abs/<doi>), each checked against the
volume Crossref gives for that DOI.

identifiers.why: Escamilla, Grudić & Rosen (2026). Published in ApJ; ORCID carries only the DOI, so the bibliography had no ADS link.

Rosen et al. (2017), HARM². ORCID carries only the DOI; the bibcode (checked: JCoPh 330, 924, 2017 — matches the DOI's volume/page) also lets the featured card resolve this paper's abstract by identifier rather than its differing title.
ORCID carries the preprint bibcode 2025arXiv251203129R; SciX resolves the DOI to the published record.

identifiers.title: What Sets the Initial Rotation Rates of Massive Stars?
identifiers.why: ORCID carries the journal's all-caps title; casing as SciX and the CV give it.
